# core/bitmap.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/bitmap.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Allocation maps.

An allocation map says for each entry (a disk block, a page, a slot)
whether it is in use. Two layouts, with the same operations and the
same guarantees:

- A `Bytes` with one byte per entry (`map_*`): 0 is free, anything else
  is in use. Handy when the map lives in a buffer that is also written
  to disk byte by byte.
- `Bits` (`bits_*`): 64 entries packed in each `u64` word, a set bit
  meaning in use. An eighth of the memory, and a search skips a word
  whose 64 entries are all taken in one comparison.

The functions work on a range `lo..hi`, so a map can reserve its first
entries (a disk's superblock and tables) and be longer than the part in
use. Searches start at a hint and wrap around, so that allocation does
not rescan the full prefix every time.

What is proved: every index is in bounds; a search returns a free entry
in `lo..hi`, or `hi` only when every entry in `lo..hi` is in use; taking
an entry marks exactly that entry and changes no other (for `Bits`,
`has_bit` states this bit by bit); the free count is at most the size of
the range.

`import "core/bitmap.bastio";`

| [`map_find_free`](#map_find_free) | A free entry of `lo..hi`, searching from `hint` up to `hi` and then from `lo` up to `hint` (a hint outside the range starts at `lo`). |
| [`map_take`](#map_take) | Finds a free entry as `map_find_free` does and marks it in use (byte 1). |
| [`map_give`](#map_give) | Marks entry `i` free. |
| [`map_fill`](#map_fill) | Marks entries `lo..hi` with `v` (0 free, anything else in use). |
| [`map_count_free`](#map_count_free) | The number of free entries in `lo..hi`. |
| [`bits_test`](#bits_test) | Is entry `i` in use? |
| [`bits_set`](#bits_set) | Marks entry `i` in use. |

| [`bits_new`](#bits_new) | `n` entries, all clear. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `Bits`

```bastio
struct Bits { w: Vec[u64], n: u64 }
```

A packed bitmap of `n` entries, 64 to a word: entry i is bit i % 64 of
word i / 64. A set bit means taken.

## Functions

### `map_is_free`

```bastio
fn map_is_free(m: &Bytes, i: u64) -> bool
  requires i < blen(m)
  ensures result == (bget(m, i) == 0)
```

Is entry `i` free?

### `map_find_free`

```bastio
fn map_find_free(m: &Bytes, lo: u64, hi: u64, hint: u64) -> u64
  requires lo <= hi && hi <= blen(m)
  ensures result <= hi
  ensures result < hi ==> lo <= result && bget(m, result) == 0
  ensures result == hi ==> map_full(m, lo, hi)
```

A free entry of `lo..hi`, searching from `hint` up to `hi` and then
from `lo` up to `hint` (a hint outside the range starts at `lo`).
Returns `hi` when every entry is in use.

### `map_take`

```bastio
fn map_take(m: &mut Bytes, lo: u64, hi: u64, hint: u64) -> u64
  requires lo <= hi && hi <= blen(m)
  ensures result <= hi
  ensures result < hi ==> lo <= result && bget(old(m), result) == 0 && bget(m, result) == 1
  ensures map_same_but(m, old(m), result)
  ensures result == hi ==> map_full(m, lo, hi)
```

Finds a free entry as `map_find_free` does and marks it in use (byte
1). Returns it, or `hi` when every entry is in use (then `m` is
unchanged).

Example:

```bastio
// A map of 16 disk blocks, one byte each; blocks 0 and 1 are reserved.
let mut m = balloc(16);
map_fill(&mut m, 0, 2, 1);
let a = map_take(&mut m, 2, 16, 0);   // the hint is outside 2..16: start at 2
let b = map_take(&mut m, 2, 16, a);
if a == 16 || b == 16 { bfree(m); return 1; }   // full
assert bget(m, a) != 0 && 2 <= a;               // proved from the contracts
map_give(&mut m, a);
let ok = a == 2 && b == 3 && map_is_free(m, 2) && map_count_free(m, 0, 16) == 13 && map_find_free(m, 2, 16, 3) == 4;
bfree(m);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `map_give`

```bastio
fn map_give(m: &mut Bytes, i: u64)
  requires i < blen(m)
  ensures bget(m, i) == 0 && map_same_but(m, old(m), i)
```

Marks entry `i` free.

### `map_fill`

```bastio
fn map_fill(m: &mut Bytes, lo: u64, hi: u64, v: u8)
  requires lo <= hi && hi <= blen(m)
  ensures blen(m) == blen(old(m))
  ensures forall k: u64 :: lo <= k && k < hi ==> bget(m, k) == v
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < blen(m) && (k < lo || hi <= k) ==> bget(m, k) == bget(old(m), k)
```

Marks entries `lo..hi` with `v` (0 free, anything else in use).

### `map_count_free`

```bastio
fn map_count_free(m: &Bytes, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> u64
  requires lo <= hi && hi <= blen(m)
  ensures result <= hi - lo
```

The number of free entries in `lo..hi`.

### `bits_test`

```bastio
fn bits_test(b: &Bits, i: u64) -> bool
  requires bits_ok(b) && i < b.n
  ensures result == bits_at(b, i)
```

Is entry `i` in use?

### `bits_set`

```bastio
fn bits_set(b: &mut Bits, i: u64)
  requires bits_ok(b) && i < b.n
  ensures bits_ok(b) && bits_at(b, i) && bits_same_but(b, old(b), i)
```

Marks entry `i` in use.

### `bits_clear`

```bastio
fn bits_clear(b: &mut Bits, i: u64)
  requires bits_ok(b) && i < b.n
  ensures bits_ok(b) && !bits_at(b, i) && bits_same_but(b, old(b), i)
```

Marks entry `i` free.

### `bits_new`

```bastio
fn bits_new(n: u64) -> Bits
  requires n <= 1152921504606846976
  ensures bits_ok(result) && result.n == n
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < n ==> !bits_at(result, k)
```

`n` entries, all clear.

Example:

```bastio
// 100 pages, 64 to a word.
let mut b = bits_new(100);
bits_set(&mut b, 0);                       // page 0 is reserved
let p = bits_take(&mut b, 1, 100, 1);      // the first free page from 1
let q = bits_find_clear(b, 1, 100, 1);     // the next free one, not taken
if p == 100 { bits_free(b); return 1; }
assert bits_at(b, p);                      // proved: taking set it
bits_give(&mut b, p);
bits_clear(&mut b, 0);
let ok = p == 1 && q == 2 && !bits_test(b, 1) && bits_count_clear(b, 0, 100) == 100;
bits_free(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bits_grow`

```bastio
fn bits_grow(b: &mut Bits, n: u64) -> bool
  requires bits_ok(b) && b.n <= n && n <= 1152921504606846976
  ensures bits_ok(b)
  ensures result ==> b.n == n
  ensures !result ==> b.n == old(b).n && vlen(b.w) == vlen(old(b).w)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < old(b).n ==> bits_at(b, k) == bits_at(old(b), k)
  ensures result ==> (forall k: u64 :: old(b).n <= k && k < n ==> !bits_at(b, k))
```

Grows the map to `n` entries, the new ones clear, keeping every old
entry. Returns false, with the map unchanged, when memory runs out: it
never stops the program.

Example:

```bastio
let mut b = bits_new(10);
bits_set(&mut b, 3);
if !bits_grow(&mut b, 1000) {
  bits_free(b);
  return 1;   // out of memory: the map is unchanged
}
assert b.n == 1000;
let ok = bits_test(b, 3) && !bits_test(b, 999) && bits_count_clear(b, 0, 1000) == 999;
bits_free(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bits_free`

```bastio
fn bits_free(b: Bits)
```

Frees the map's storage.

### `bits_find_clear`

```bastio
fn bits_find_clear(b: &Bits, lo: u64, hi: u64, hint: u64) -> u64
  requires bits_ok(b) && lo <= hi && hi <= b.n
  ensures result <= hi
  ensures result < hi ==> lo <= result && !bits_at(b, result)
  ensures result == hi ==> bits_full(b, lo, hi)
```

The first clear entry in `lo..hi`, searching from `hint` and wrapping
around to `lo`, as `map_find_free`. Returns `hi` only when every entry
in `lo..hi` is set.

### `bits_take`

```bastio
fn bits_take(b: &mut Bits, lo: u64, hi: u64, hint: u64) -> u64
  requires bits_ok(b) && lo <= hi && hi <= b.n
  ensures bits_ok(b) && result <= hi
  ensures result < hi ==> lo <= result && !bits_at(old(b), result) && bits_at(b, result)
  ensures bits_same_but(b, old(b), result)
  ensures result == hi ==> bits_full(b, lo, hi)
```

Finds a clear entry as `bits_find_clear` does and sets it. Returns it,
or `hi` when every entry is set (then `b` is unchanged).

### `bits_give`

```bastio
fn bits_give(b: &mut Bits, i: u64)
  requires bits_ok(b) && i < b.n
  ensures bits_ok(b) && !bits_at(b, i) && bits_same_but(b, old(b), i)
```

Clears entry `i`.

### `bits_count_clear`

```bastio
fn bits_count_clear(b: &Bits, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> u64
  requires bits_ok(b) && lo <= hi && hi <= b.n
  ensures result <= hi - lo
```

The number of clear entries in `lo..hi`.

## Specification functions

### `map_full`

```bastio
spec fn map_full(m: &Bytes, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: lo <= k && k < hi ==> bget(m, k) != 0
}
```

Every entry in `lo..hi` of `m` is in use.

### `map_same_but`

```bastio
spec fn map_same_but(m: &Bytes, o: &Bytes, at: u64) -> bool {
  blen(m) == blen(o) && (forall k: u64 :: k < blen(m) && k != at ==> bget(m, k) == bget(o, k))
}
```

`m` and `o` have the same length and agree everywhere except at `at`.

### `bits_ok`

```bastio
spec fn bits_ok(b: &Bits) -> bool {
  b.n <= 64 * vlen(b.w) && b.n <= 1152921504606846976
}
```

### `bits_at`

```bastio
spec fn bits_at(b: &Bits, i: u64) -> bool {
  has_bit(vget(b.w, i / 64), i % 64)
}
```

Entry i is set.

### `bits_full`

```bastio
spec fn bits_full(b: &Bits, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: lo <= k && k < hi ==> bits_at(b, k)
}
```

Entries lo..hi are all set.

### `bits_same_but`

```bastio
spec fn bits_same_but(b: &Bits, o: &Bits, at: u64) -> bool {
  b.n == o.n && vlen(b.w) == vlen(o.w) && (forall k: u64 :: k < b.n && k != at ==> bits_at(b, k) == bits_at(o, k))
}
```

`b` and `o` differ at most in entry `at`.

## Internals

### `bits_find_clear_in`

```bastio
fn bits_find_clear_in(b: &Bits, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> u64
  requires bits_ok(b) && lo <= hi && hi <= b.n
  ensures result <= hi
  ensures result < hi ==> lo <= result && !bits_at(b, result)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: lo <= k && k < result ==> bits_at(b, k)
```

Internal: The first clear entry in lo..hi, or hi if all are set.
